key_insight: A physics-informed CNN-LSTM can forecast long-term photoluminescence degradation of perovskites from early time-series data, improving generalization to unseen materials.
engineering_relevance: This enables faster, lower-cost stability screening for perovskite solar cell materials by reducing the need for extended aging experiments.
method: Collected 86k+ photoluminescence spectra from 167 metal halide perovskites under heat and light stress.
Converted spectra into physics-informed features to make degradation behavior more interpretable.
Trained a hybrid CNN-LSTM to predict future PL intensity for samples not seen during training.
evidence_signal: The approach was evaluated on a diverse dataset of 167 perovskites and outperformed baseline benchmarks while generalizing across material groups.
watch_item: Forecast quality may depend on the representativeness of the training materials and stress conditions, so extrapolation to new chemistries or test protocols should be validated carefully.
paper_title: Physics-informed time-series forecasting of perovskite photoluminescence stability
